newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gabon's Bongo calls for conference on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Gabon's Bongo calls for conference on Zaire.

text.p: Gabonese President Omar Bongo has proposed an international conference to try to restore peace in eastern Zaire, where more than a million mostly Hutu refugees caught in cross-border fighting face disaster.
"If I am needed to discuss with the warring parties, I am ready to go," Bongo told the French newspaper Le Figaro in an interview published on Monday.

"But for such a serious problem, the heads of all the neighbouring states would need to meet. An even wider conference could be called as what is happening today in Zaire could happen anywhere in Africa tomorrow," he added.
A two-week lightning offensive in eastern Zaire by Tutsi rebels, some backed by government forces from neighbouring Rwanda, has thrown Zaire's army into disarray and left refugees cut off.
Bongo said rebels appeared set to create a Tutsi homeland in Zaire's Kivu province and Kinshasa had the right to drive them out.
"I think Zaire is entitled to drive them out. Why let the Zaire Tutsis stay if they bring war against the country that has been their host?" he asked.
Bongo said that any attempt to solve the ethnic conflict would be shortlived because Hutus were a majority in both Rwanda and Burundi, but Tutsis were better organised militarily.
Elections would always lead to coups, he said.
"If these people wanted peace, they would have said to each other: "You came to power through bayonets, I came to power through the ballot box. Let us share the presidency.'
"At the moment...the line is rather: "Go away, so I can take your place'," he said.

The Gabon leader rejected a U.S. proposal for an African peace force to intervene in African conflicts. He said such a proposal was "a dream" as the Organisation of African Unity did not have the means to raise an army.
